  - [CLAIM-917](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-917.md) — On the narrow reading of the dependence rule, a constraint the capacity depends on but the agent does not produce is a condition, not a member of K, so a capacity whose realizing constraints all lie outside the agent is not the agent's to maintain *(Proposed)*
- [CLAIM-947](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-947.md) — In the coupled meaning–influence model of two hypotheses and two specialists, with conferral a moving average toward a softmax of agreement with the current meaning, the symmetric state is unstable exactly when gσ² > 2(1 − φ(1 − ε)): the conferral memory and the meaning rate set how fast capture comes, not whether it comes or where it settles *(Active)*
  - [CLAIM-1000](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1000.md) — In two coupled meaning–influence institutions, each stable alone, with nonnegative channels by which each one's meaning moves the other's evidence or conferral, the symmetric state of the pair is unstable exactly when the round-trip gain exceeds one, which for the built institutions is (θ + σ_E ω)(χ + σ_P ψ) > Δ_E Δ_P with Δ_i each institution's own margin; the meaning rates and the conferral memories cancel, and each institution's inner loop enters only through its margin *(Active)*
    - [CLAIM-1021](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1021.md) — If an evaluated party's resources scale how strongly the evaluator's conferral answers agreement, rather than tilting it toward one side, they enter the two-institution meaning–influence model only beyond first order at the symmetric state: they leave the linear symmetry-breaking condition unchanged, yet they capture the evaluator's reading below that condition from a large enough push, toward the side the resources favour only, even when the evaluator's evidence is independent of the party *(Active)*
    - [CLAIM-1202](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1202.md) — In the two-institution meaning–influence model, the loop between an evaluator and the party it evaluates can capture the evaluator's reading when each institution is stable alone, when neither has a loop inside it, and when the evaluator's conferral reads no interpretation at all; informational independence does not prevent it while a resource channel runs, and what does is a return channel too weak to close the loop, the evaluator's reading not moving the party's standing or evidence *(Active)*
      - [CLAIM-1024](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1024.md) — A system's ability to correct itself depends not simply on having critics or feedback but on how evidence, evaluation and authority are coupled, and on what the system is prevented from rewriting or rejecting *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-1029, CLAIM-1183, CLAIM-1194, CLAIM-342

### From If a map approximately intertwines two operators, with defects E_A = ΦA − A′Φ and E_B = ΦB − B′Φ, then Φ[A,B] − [A′,B′]Φ = A′E_B + E_A B − B′E_A − E_B A, so the commutator is carried to within (‖A‖ + ‖A′‖)‖E_B‖ + (‖B‖ + ‖B′‖)‖E_A‖

- [CLAIM-373](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-373.md) — If a map approximately intertwines two operators, with defects E_A = ΦA − A′Φ and E_B = ΦB − B′Φ, then Φ[A,B] − [A′,B′]Φ = A′E_B + E_A B − B′E_A − E_B A, so the commutator is carried to within (‖A‖ + ‖A′‖)‖E_B‖ + (‖B‖ + ‖B′‖)‖E_A‖ *(Active)*

### From Continuous predicates are test functions, test functions determine measures, and so a self can be a continuous mess rather than a countable collection of perspectives

- [CLAIM-1112](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1112.md) — Continuous predicates are test functions, test functions determine measures, and so a self can be a continuous mess rather than a countable collection of perspectives *(Proposed)*
  - [CLAIM-1055](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1055.md) — A self may be better modelled as a historically evolving, measure-valued organization of dispositions than as a discrete collection of perspectives: perspectives are overlapping, intervention-dependent structures in it, their separability is set by the observer's test functions and the metric they induce, and its unity lies in maintained causal relations, not in one privileged perspective or a partition into mutually singular parts *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-1167, CLAIM-1186
- [CLAIM-1167](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1167.md) — Perspectives given as graded participation functions on a common measure overlap by the integral of their pointwise minimum, which is zero exactly when the measures they carve out are mutually singular and, for probability densities, equals one minus their total-variation distance, so separation of perspectives comes by degrees and need not be a partition *(Active)*
  - [CLAIM-1096](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1096.md) — Graded predicates on a measure space, identified almost everywhere and ordered pointwise, form a distributive lattice under minimum and maximum whose L¹ distance is the metric of the valuation p ↦ ∫p dμ, while the concept lattice of a thresholded incidence can be any complete lattice and need not be distributive, so the two lattices a theory of overlapping perspectives might use are different objects *(Active)*
    - [CLAIM-1101](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1101.md) — Linear tests are not closed under pointwise minimum or maximum, so a lattice whose concepts each have a linear test cannot in general give its meets and joins linear tests; this does not tell against Xiong's lattice representation hypothesis as stated, whose meet is already an intersection of half-spaces and not a direction *(Active)*
      - [CLAIM-1035](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1035.md) — A self-like organization may be realized over a continuous measure of dispositions, with linear representations giving locally accessible tests, lattices organizing the implications and overlaps among those tests, and causal dynamics deciding which of the resulting distinctions are maintained and consequential, so that discrete perspectives are a property of the observational and organizational regime rather than a primitive of the dispositional space *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-1055, CLAIM-1096, CLAIM-1163
- [CLAIM-1186](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1186.md) — A response profile that is positive, linear and normalized in the continuous test is a probability measure, and a declared family of tests turns the largest disagreement between two such measures into a pseudometric, which is a metric exactly when the family separates measures, so that observational equivalence under the family is distance zero *(Active)*
  - [CLAIM-1163](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1163.md) — Linear tests of a representation see a distribution only through its mean representation: their largest disagreement is the dual norm of the difference of means, so two distributions with one mean, as a point mass at 0 and an even split between −1 and 1, are at distance zero under every linear test and are told apart by a single nonlinear one *(Active)*

### From A protected beacon's miscalibration is unidentifiable from inside the sensor network by a symmetry: a world whose beacon reports z* + d and a world whose beacon is correct, with the target, the beacon placements and every sensor bias shifted (z + d, z* + d, b_i - A_i d), give every report identically, so no revision that uses only the network's reports can find d, and correcting it needs evidence that breaks the symmetry from outside

- [CLAIM-1125](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1125.md) — A protected beacon's miscalibration is unidentifiable from inside the sensor network by a symmetry: a world whose beacon reports z* + d and a world whose beacon is correct, with the target, the beacon placements and every sensor bias shifted (z + d, z* + d, b_i - A_i d), give every report identically, so no revision that uses only the network's reports can find d, and correcting it needs evidence that breaks the symmetry from outside *(Active)*
  - [CLAIM-1111](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1111.md) — The regress of anchors, in which a protected anchor's own error needs a further anchor to correct it, resembles Gödel's incompleteness *(Proposed)* — through [ARG-233](../record/arguments.d/ARG-233.md) — also argued from CLAIM-1185
  - [CLAIM-1143](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1143.md) — An independent physical witness certifies every difference among the channels that read it and never their common mode: if k channels each read the same placed points with an offset of their own, their reports identify every difference between offsets and leave one shift of all offsets and points together unidentified, however many channels there are; so the regress of anchors ends at a witness only together with a standard fixed by definition, which is how measurement ends it, and an error every channel shares stays invisible *(Proposed)* — through [ARG-234](../record/arguments.d/ARG-234.md)
    - [CLAIM-1151](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1151.md) — Physics is better read as a quotient of mathematics with a coordination than as a subset of it: mathematically distinct models that no observation can tell apart are one physical situation, so physical content is what survives identification up to the symmetries observation cannot break; the same mathematics describes different physics until definitions coordinate it with phenomena, and those definitions are not mathematics; and what can be observed is relative to the channels available, so the quotient moves as instruments do *(Proposed)* — through [ARG-235](../record/arguments.d/ARG-235.md) — also rests on CLAIM-1125; also argued from CLAIM-1125
- [CLAIM-1185](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1185.md) — What a system is prevented from rewriting or rejecting can bound what it can correct as well as enable correction: in the record's simulated sensor network a protected beacon that is itself miscalibrated drives the network's error to the beacon's own error while keeping it internally consistent, the network's own revision does not lower it, and in the runs it fell only when a further, rarer protected channel revised the beacon's calibration, at that channel's rate *(Active)*
  - [CLAIM-1282](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1282.md) — Correction is relative to the anchors it answers to: an anchor a system can neither rewrite nor reject imports its own errors whole, and the system can correct them only through a further protected channel, an anchor of their own *(Proposed)*

### From A model's parameter complexity and its behavioural complexity come apart: when its predictions depend on a few stiff combinations of parameters and barely on the rest, it can be hard to fit and still predictive, so simplicity can belong to how a system responds to observation rather than to its mechanism

- [CLAIM-820](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-820.md) — A model's parameter complexity and its behavioural complexity come apart: when its predictions depend on a few stiff combinations of parameters and barely on the rest, it can be hard to fit and still predictive, so simplicity can belong to how a system responds to observation rather than to its mechanism *(Proposed)*
  - [CLAIM-1174](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1174.md) — A self may be considered as a sloppy mess of connected perspectives in the technical sense of sloppy: an organization of many coupled degrees of freedom whose responses to the affordable probes depend on a few stiff combinations of them and barely on the rest, so that it can be richly differentiated within and still appear low-dimensional, and which of its differences show depends on the probes *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-861
- [CLAIM-861](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-861.md) — A coarse-grained description, the sloppiness of a model and the emergence of one level from another are each defined only relative to a chosen set of observables and a demanded precision, and given that choice the dynamics fix the rest: which partition is causal, which parameter combinations are stiff, and whether one description emerges from another *(Proposed)*

### From Preserving an inherited arrangement's structure does not preserve the capacities it realizes, since what an arrangement realizes depends on its environment, and keeping it is itself a choice with developmental consequences whose costs fall on particular parties: persistence shows that an arrangement has been reproducible, not what makes it reproducible or whether its reproduction is justified, and the status quo is not a zero-cost baseline

- [CLAIM-1253](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1253.md) — Preserving an inherited arrangement's structure does not preserve the capacities it realizes, since what an arrangement realizes depends on its environment, and keeping it is itself a choice with developmental consequences whose costs fall on particular parties: persistence shows that an arrangement has been reproducible, not what makes it reproducible or whether its reproduction is justified, and the status quo is not a zero-cost baseline *(Proposed)*
- [CLAIM-1279](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1279.md) — An expectation is an operative norm rather than a prediction when a discrepancy is met by bringing the behaviour back into line with the expectation instead of revising the expectation to fit the behaviour; which response a discrepancy gets, adaptation, enforcement, accommodation or revision, is the work of normative governance *(Proposed)*
- [CLAIM-1281](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1281.md) — Under reversal of a social attribution with its grounds held fixed, every response splits uniquely into a part that reverses with the attribution and a part that does not: conformity and defiance lie wholly in the first and a response governed by the grounds alone wholly in the second, so the size of the reversing part, not its direction, measures how far the attribution sets the terms of response; the transformation type records only which parts are present, and reversing the attribution together with its grounds measures nothing *(Active)*
  - [CLAIM-1342](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1342.md) — In the toy models filed from assistants' exchanges, the verbal conclusion drawn from a model often reads a parameter as the concept it was introduced to stand for, so checking a model's numbers is not enough: each parameter's reading has to be checked before a conclusion is read off it *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-1284, CLAIM-1324
- [CLAIM-1284](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1284.md) — A norm can be stabilized by the reliance it attracts: compliance makes a practice predictable, others specialize around it, and their stake in its continuation funds its maintenance, which raises compliance, so a practice established past a threshold can persist where a weakly established one would not, and can outlast a weakening of the reasons that first supported it *(Proposed)*
  - [CLAIM-1318](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1318.md) — A norm's original justification and its baseline support come apart: the justification can vanish while the norm keeps support from replacement rationales and from the interests it serves, so a norm that outlasts its justification need not have outlasted its support, and a bistable norm ends by a push past its threshold rather than by fading *(Proposed)*
    - [CLAIM-1294](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1294.md) — Strong preservationist conservatism is deficient where it treats preserving an established arrangement as preserving the capacities it realizes, or historical endurance as a general presumption of adequacy, counting the dangers of reform and not the costs of continued operation; conservatism's valid insight, that institutions store work and knowledge no one holds explicitly, supports caution but not that conflation *(Proposed)* — through [ARG-254](../record/arguments.d/ARG-254.md) — also rests on CLAIM-1253
- [CLAIM-1324](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1324.md) — In A11's model of confirmation feedback, where an agent adds each observation's log-likelihood ratio a·y to its log odds ℓ while ℓ tilts which observations it samples, q(y | ℓ) ∝ p(y)exp(κℓy), and never corrects for the tilt, the unbiased state is unstable for every κ > 0; the threshold κ > 2/3 shown with it comes from the illustration's decay factor 0.92, and a decay λ puts the threshold at κ = λ/a *(Active)*
- [CLAIM-738](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-738.md) — Rights, demands and commitments are distinct and none establishes another: a right does not depend on being demanded or on anyone's commitment to it, a demand's being asserted, maintained or recognized gives it no warrant, and a commitment is neither an obligation nor an authorization, while an obligation persists without commitment; each passage between them, a right generating a demand or a valid undertaking generating a right, needs its own warrant *(Active)*
  - [CLAIM-1212](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1212.md) — Repetition and reliance can turn a discretionary contribution into an operative obligation, whose withdrawal is treated as a breach, with no agreement ever made; but being expected, being relied on, being committed and owing are distinct, and reliance makes something owed only under a further principle, such as one about reliance knowingly induced *(Proposed)*
    - [CLAIM-1326](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1326.md) — An implicit contract's operative obligation, once normalized by the recipient's reliance, can be held by that reliance past the provider's original reasons for the contribution, where the provider cannot cheaply exit *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-1279, CLAIM-1284

### From In a comparison of preserving an arrangement against transforming it, uncertainty about the alternative's costs together with an irreversible transition cost gives waiting to learn an option value, so transforming can beat preserving in expectation while waiting beats both; when the status quo irreversibly erodes the capacity to transform, the ranking can reverse, so symmetric scrutiny requires pricing irreversibility on both sides

- [CLAIM-1246](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1246.md) — In a comparison of preserving an arrangement against transforming it, uncertainty about the alternative's costs together with an irreversible transition cost gives waiting to learn an option value, so transforming can beat preserving in expectation while waiting beats both; when the status quo irreversibly erodes the capacity to transform, the ranking can reverse, so symmetric scrutiny requires pricing irreversibility on both sides *(Active)*
  - [CLAIM-1266](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1266.md) — Conservatism as its theorists state it is a presumption under uncertainty, not a conflation of persistence with value: it rests on premises the critique itself grants, that an inherited arrangement's dependencies are only partly legible and that destroying them can be irreversible, and it places the burden of proof on change while conceding that conservation requires correction; what survives of the critique is who bears the cost of waiting, and that keeping a structure is not keeping its goods *(Proposed)*

### From A luria record is an atlas of charts over an inquiry

- [CLAIM-1335](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1335.md) — A luria record is an atlas of charts over an inquiry *(Proposed)*
  - [CLAIM-1260](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1260.md) — A series of blog posts can be laid out as a route through the space of hyperarticles over the record, chosen as an orbit or as a geodesic *(Proposed)*
- [CLAIM-1337](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1337.md) — Noticing a distinction that keeps a class stable, so that instances of one kind are still recognized as that kind across changes of context, presentation or application and are not confused with a neighbouring kind, is one way an inquiry progresses *(Proposed)*
  - [CLAIM-1277](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1277.md) — A distinction advances an inquiry by stabilizing the classification of its objects across changes of context, representation or use: operations that had been conflated can then be evaluated apart, and conclusions and maintenance obligations carried across contexts without silently changing what they refer to; stabilizing a class does not show that the class is correct, that its boundaries are adequate or that keeping it is worth its cost *(Proposed)*
    - [CLAIM-1297](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-1297.md) — An evolving inquiry can be understood as an atlas of partial representations whose objects and relations must stay identifiable across changes of perspective, purpose and grammar; progress can consist in finding distinctions or transformations that improve compatibility among the representations, and since their adequacy is itself under inquiry the atlas must be governed rather than assumed fixed, so class stability is a relation across representations and not a demand that one classification stay unchanged *(Proposed)* — also rests on CLAIM-1335

### From Resolving a singularity by blow-up reparametrizes the states and adds no observation, so it cannot make indistinguishable states distinguishable: every point over a singular point gives the same distribution, and the Fisher information can stay degenerate there; what the resolution buys is a normal form for the divergence, and so the learning coefficient

- [CLAIM-305](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-305.md) — Resolving a singularity by blow-up reparametrizes the states and adds no observation, so it cannot make indistinguishable states distinguishable: every point over a singular point gives the same distribution, and the Fisher information can stay degenerate there; what the resolution buys is a normal form for the divergence, and so the learning coefficient *(Active)*
  - [CLAIM-813](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-813.md) — Sloppiness and singularity are different properties of a statistical model: sloppiness is a spread of small but nonzero Fisher eigenvalues in a regular model, singularity is rank loss on a stratum of parameter space, so a model can be sloppy everywhere and singular nowhere or singular everywhere with no spread, and at a singular point the Fisher spectrum does not give the learning coefficient *(Proposed)*
    - [CLAIM-812](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-812.md) — Sloppiness and singular strata meet in two places and part in one: a sloppy eigenvalue near a stratum measures the squared distance to it, and at a finite sample size a direction too sloppy to resolve contributes to the learning coefficient no more than a flat one; they part in how the coefficient moves with sample size, rising about ½ for each direction resolved in a regular sloppy model toward d/2, and held below d/2 at every size in a singular one *(Proposed)*
      - [CLAIM-808](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-808.md) — Watanabe's stratification of a model's parameter space connects to the hyperribbon account of sloppy models *(Proposed)* — through [ARG-138](../record/arguments.d/ARG-138.md) — also argued from CLAIM-813
  - [CLAIM-823](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-823.md) — Alternative reading (b) of the owner's suggestion on singularities: a phase transition in learning is a change in which singular region of parameter space dominates, as the sample size grows, between regions that fit differently and have different learning coefficients, and resolution of singularities is the tool that computes those coefficients *(Proposed)* — through [ARG-132](../record/arguments.d/ARG-132.md)

### From Material interdependence couples parties' outcomes without fixing the perspective that organizes the coupling: the same dependence can be organized as mutual opportunity, as competitive vulnerability or as coercive leverage, so interdependence makes for peace to the extent that cooperation also changes which interests the parties' institutions recognize and who holds influence over them, and payoff coupling alone does not settle which

- [CLAIM-428](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-428.md) — Material interdependence couples parties' outcomes without fixing the perspective that organizes the coupling: the same dependence can be organized as mutual opportunity, as competitive vulnerability or as coercive leverage, so interdependence makes for peace to the extent that cooperation also changes which interests the parties' institutions recognize and who holds influence over them, and payoff coupling alone does not settle which *(Proposed)*
  - [CLAIM-690](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-690.md) — Whichever way a whole and its part depend on each other, the same magnitude of dependence can run either way, and what sorts it is who controls the terms on which it is met, exit, renegotiation and the conditions of supply, while the magnitude and the integration that produced it set only how much rides on it: with the part able to withdraw or renegotiate, the whole's need of it becomes the part's hold on its terms; with the terms at an agent's discretion, the same need gives the part none, and the part's own dependence becomes vulnerability to that agent, on whom, under a principle grounding obligations in such vulnerability, the strengthened responsibility falls *(Proposed)* — through [ARG-110](../record/arguments.d/ARG-110.md) — also argued from CLAIM-671
- [CLAIM-671](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-671.md) — Where an organizational transformation increases a constituent's vulnerability to the discretionary choices of a responsible agent, and that vulnerability grounds special obligations under an independently justified principle, the transformation can strengthen that agent's responsibilities toward the constituent *(Proposed)*

### From That no single institution can bring about a remedy does not imply that no combination of them can: the institutions able together to realize a corrective outcome need include none able alone, so a true statement of unilateral inability is not a statement that the outcome is unattainable

- [CLAIM-457](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-457.md) — That no single institution can bring about a remedy does not imply that no combination of them can: the institutions able together to realize a corrective outcome need include none able alone, so a true statement of unilateral inability is not a statement that the outcome is unattainable *(Active)*
  - [CLAIM-688](../record/claims.d/CLAIM-688.md) — A collective's capacity to decline a feasible technology, which is part of its self-direction over that technology, can depend more on the competition it is in than on its own organization: where forgoing the technology leaves a collective dependent on rivals that adopt it, none of the competitors can decline it alone, and the capacity exists, if anywhere, in coordination among them *(Active)*
